description: Ask the web a question and get back ranked results: title, URL and the snippet the index holds. They are read live off a real search front through a residential exit, never a reseller's cache. `country` picks both the exit and the market, so `br` returns what somebody in Brazil would see. Narrow to your own list of hosts with `includeDomains`, ask for `topic: "news"` when you want dated journalism or `topic: "images"` when you want pictures, and add `answer: true` when you want a paragraph written over the results instead of writing it yourself. To read a result, pass its URL to `scrape`.

answer.description: Also write a short paragraph answering the query from the results, in the query's language. Costs one extra credit; leave it off when your own model reads the snippets.

includeDomains.description: Only results on these hosts, bare (`linkedin.com`). Subdomains are included. Asked of the search front AND enforced on the answer, so what comes back is on your list whatever the front did with it. With `topic: "images"` it takes one host.

limit.description: How many results to hand back at most, 1–20. Billed per 10, so asking for more than 10 costs a second row. Fewer can come back than you asked for: an index has what it has, and `includeDomains` filters what it returns.

proxy.description: Where the search leaves from. `country` picks the exit AND the market the front answers for. `br` gets Brazilian results in Portuguese.

country.description: Where the call should look like it comes from, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (`us`, `br`). Name one and the managed pool leaves from that country. Leave it out and the page sees a US browser, from an address we pick. A scrape or a map on the managed pool makes one exception: a site whose address ends in `.br`, `.de`, `.es`, `.fr`, `.it`, `.jp`, `.nl`, `.pl` or `.uk` is read from its own country. The browser's clock and languages follow the country on every pool.

pool.description: Which exit to leave through. "residential" is the managed pool, metered by the megabyte; "custom" is your own proxy, free on every plan, bytes never billed.

server.description: Your own proxy, `http(s)://[user:pass@]host:port`. Required for pool "custom", refused for the managed one.

query.description: What to search for, in plain words: the same thing you would type.

timeRange.description: Only pages from the last day, week, month or year. Absent is any time.

topic.description: What kind of results. "general" is the web; "news" is dated journalism, and the only topic that reliably carries `publishedAt`; "images" is pictures: each result is the page that shows one, with the picture's own address, a thumbnail and its size in `image`. Pictures the engine marks as adult are left out.

name: search
title: Search the web
